question: How did Alphabet's full-year 2026 CapEx guidance evolve from the Q4 2025 call to the Q3 2026 call?
goldAnswer: $175-185B (Q4 2025), raised to $180-190B (Q1 2026, includes Intersect), raised to $195-205B (Q2), unchanged at $195-205B (Q3).
answer:
Alphabet's full-year 2026 CapEx guidance evolved as follows:

- In the FY2025 Q4 call, the CapEx guidance for 2026 was initially set in the range of **$175 billion to $185 billion** [1].
- In the FY2026 Q1 call, this guidance was updated to **$180 billion to $190 billion** [2].
- By the FY2026 Q2 call, the CapEx guidance was further increased to **$195 billion to $205 billion** [3].
- The FY2026 Q3 call maintained the CapEx guidance at **$195 billion to $205 billion** [4].

Thus, the CapEx guidance increased from $175-$185 billion to $195-$205 billion over the course of the quarters.

Speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google
First, in terms of revenues, we're pleased with the overall momentum of the business. At current spot rates, we would expect to see an FX tailwind toward consolidated revenues in Q1. However, the volatility in exchange rates could affect the impact of FX on Q1 revenues.

In Google Services, we expect growth to be driven by ongoing innovation in the user experience, as well as improved ROI for advertisers, keeping in mind the normal seasonal pattern for advertising revenue.

In Google Cloud, we're seeing significant demand for our products and services, which we expect to continue to drive strong growth, despite the tight supply environment we're operating in.

Moving to investments, the investments we have been making in AI are already translating to strong performance across the business, as you've seen in our financial results. Our successful execution, coupled with strong performance, reinforces our conviction to make the investments required to further capitalize on the AI opportunity.

For the full year 2026, we expect CapEx to be in the range of $175 billion to $185 billion, with investments ramping over the course of the year.

We're investing in AI compute capacity to support frontier model development by Google DeepMind, ongoing efforts to improve the user experience, and drive higher advertiser ROI in Google Services, significant Cloud customer demand, as well as strategic investments in Other Bets.

Keep in mind that the availability of supply, pricing of components, and timing of cash payments can cause some variability in the reported CapEx number.

In terms of expenses, as we've discussed on previous calls, the significant increase in our investments in technical infrastructure will continue to put pressure on the P&L in the form of higher depreciation expense and related data centers' operations costs such as energy.

In 2025, depreciation increased by nearly $6 billion, or 38%, from $15.3 billion in 2024, to $21.1 billion in 2025. Given the increase in our CapEx investments in recent years, we expect the growth rate in 2026 depreciation to accelerate in Q1, and meaningfully increase for the full year.

We're also planning to continue hiring in key investment areas, such as AI and Cloud.

In 2025, our teams delivered amazing innovation, executing with a high level of discipline and velocity. These efforts provided great experiences for consumers and outstanding performance for creators, partners, and enterprise customers driving strong revenue growth.

Other income and expenses was $3.2 billion, primarily due to unrealized gains in our non-marketable equity securities portfolio.

REDMOND, Wash. — July 29, 2026 — Microsoft Corp. today announced the following results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, as compared to the corresponding period of last fiscal year:

• Revenue was $90.0 billion and increased 18% (up 17% in constant currency)

Section: Revenue Recognition
Revenues are recognized when control of the promised goods or services is transferred to our customers, and the collectibility of an amount that we expect in exchange for those goods or services is probable. Sales and other similar taxes are excluded from revenues.

Google advertising revenues consist of revenues from:

•Google Search and other properties, including revenues from traffic generated by search distribution partners who use Google.com as their default search in browsers, toolbars, etc. and other Google owned and operated properties like Gmail, Google Maps, and Google Play;

•YouTube properties; and

•Google Network properties, including revenues from Google Network properties participating in AdMob, AdSense, and Google Ad Manager.

Our customers generally purchase advertising inventory through Google Ads, Google Ad Manager, Google Display & Video 360, and Google Marketing Platform, among others.

We offer advertising by delivering both performance and brand advertising. We recognize revenues for performance advertising when a user engages with the advertisement. For brand advertising, we recognize revenues when the ad is displayed, or a user views the ad.

For ads placed on Google Network properties, we evaluate whether we are the principal (i.e., report revenues on a gross basis) or agent (i.e., report revenues on a net basis). Generally, we report advertising revenues for ads placed on Google Network properties on a gross basis, that is, the amounts billed to our customers are recorded as revenues, and amounts paid to Google Network partners are recorded as cost of revenues. Where we are the principal, we control the advertising inventory before it is transferred to our customers. Our control is evidenced by our sole ability to monetize the advertising inventory before it is transferred to our customers and is further supported by us being primarily responsible to our customers and having a level of discretion in establishing pricing.

Google subscriptions, platforms, and devices revenues consist of revenues from:

•platforms, which primarily include revenues from Google Play sales of apps and in-app purchases;

•devices, which primarily include sales of the Pixel family of devices; and

•other products and services.

Subscription revenues are recognized ratably over the period of the subscription, primarily monthly. We report revenues from Google Play sales of apps and in-app purchases on a net basis because our performance obligation is to facilitate a transaction between app developers and end users for which we earn a service fee.

[GOOGL | FY2026 Q2 | FORM_10Q]
Section: Revenue Recognition
Google Cloud revenues consist of revenues from:

•Google Cloud Platform primarily generates consumption-based fees and subscriptions for infrastructure, platform, and other services. These services provide access to solutions such as artificial intelligence (AI) offerings including our enterprise AI infrastructure, Vertex AI platform, and Gemini Enterprise; cybersecurity offerings; and data and analytics solutions.

•Google Workspace includes subscriptions for cloud-based communication and collaboration tools for enterprises, such as Gmail, Docs, Calendar, Drive, and Meet, with integrated features like Gemini for Google Workspace.

•Product sales, primarily the sale of TPU systems.

•Other enterprise services.

Our cloud services are generally provided on either a consumption or subscription basis and may have contract terms longer than a year. Revenues related to cloud services provided on a consumption basis are recognized when the customer utilizes the services, based on the quantity of services consumed using the relative standalone selling price allocation. Revenues related to cloud services provided on a subscription basis are recognized over the contract term as the customer receives and consumes the benefits of the cloud services.

Our Google Cloud product sales generally consist of the sale of TPU systems comprising hardware, software, installation, support, and extended warranty services. Customer arrangements may also include options which are accounted for as rights of return. Product sales revenue from hardware, net of estimated allowances for returns, and software is recognized generally when control of the hardware is transferred to the customer. Installation, support, and extended warranty services revenue are recognized ratably over the service period or as services are performed.

Section: 2026 Q3 Earnings Call
Speaker: Thomas Kurian, SVP and CEO, Google Cloud
To address the question on the rate of growth of Cloud, our Google Cloud segment delivered record growth in the third quarter with Cloud revenues up 103% to $30.7 billion.

The strongest growth contributor was Google Cloud Platform, with strength in both AI and Core GCP. So GCP accounted for the vast majority of revenue generated in Q3. And Cloud revenue growth, excluding the impact of TPU system sales, was again very, very strong.

Demand was also strong across our product lines. So we see three things going on.

One, as people use Gemini, we see revenue growth from Gemini itself; but we also see that as people use Gemini, it drives growth in other parts of our portfolio. For instance, as they build agents, they use compute to perform a task, and so they buy compute. They use storage to store memories of the agent. Database to serve up what's called context for the agent to reason on. And obviously given all the cybersecurity threats, we are seeing strong growth in our cybersecurity portfolio.

So we are confident about our growth and the diversity in our growth. We're also seeing new customers buy into GCP and exhilarating growth in new customer adoptions, so we also see that as a growth factor for us.

And we're always -- at any point in time, we could obviously serve a lot more demand with capacity, but we are managing all of these parameters and growth carefully.

Section: Trends in Our Business and Financial Effect
The following long-term trends have contributed to the results of our consolidated operations, and we anticipate that they will continue to affect our future results:

•As we continue to grow our business and meet the evolving behaviors and needs of our users and customers, our revenue growth and mix along with our cost and margin profiles are being influenced by a number of factors, including:

Expanded AI Offerings in our Products and Services: The continuing evolution of the online world has contributed to the growth of our business. We expect that this evolution, including user engagement with AI products and services, will continue to benefit our business and our revenues. As we continue to incorporate AI into our products and services, such as with AI Overviews and AI Mode in Search, and with enterprise AI solutions on our Google Cloud Platform, we may monetize differently than our historical consumer and enterprise offerings which could affect revenue growth rates and margin trends. When developing new products and services we generally focus first on user experience and then on monetization. At the same time, we face increasing competition, including from other developers and providers of AI products and services, which may affect our revenues.

Increasing Revenues Beyond Advertising: Revenues from cloud, consumer subscriptions, platforms, and devices, which may have differing characteristics than our advertising revenues, have grown over time. Certain of these revenues have been growing at a rate higher than our advertising revenues, becoming a larger percentage of our consolidated revenues, and we expect this trend to continue. The margins on these revenues vary significantly and are generally lower than the margins on our advertising revenues.

Increased Investment in Technical Infrastructure: We continue to invest in capital expenditures as we scale our technical infrastructure, in particular for AI, to meet the demand of our users and enterprise customers and to support research internally. We invested heavily in capital expenditures in 2025 and in 2026, we expect to significantly increase, relative to 2025, our investment in our technical infrastructure, including servers and network equipment, and data centers. The costs associated with operating our technical infrastructure - depreciation, energy, equipment, and network capacity - are expected to significantly increase as developing and serving AI offerings require more compute power than our historical consumer and enterprise offerings. While our technical infrastructure costs increase, we expect to continue to drive efficiencies in our data centers, for example, through the design of our AI models and our TPU and GPU-based technical infrastructure.

Continued Investment in Intellectual Property through R&D and Acquisitions: We continue to make significant research and development investments in areas of strategic focus as we seek to develop new, innovative offerings, and improve our existing offerings across our businesses. Acquisitions and strategic investments remain important elements in our use of capital and contribute to the breadth and depth of our offerings, expand our expertise in engineering and other functional areas, and build strong partnerships around strategic initiatives.

[META | FY2026 Q3 | TRANSCRIPT]
Speaker: Susan Li, CFO
Meta One is rolling out gradually with more than 50

features across Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp, including Meta Business Agent and Meta AI, and has surpassed 15 million subscriptions and trials to date. The core experience across our apps and Meta AI will remain free, while subscriptions offer more specialized capabilities and expanded AI usage.

Beyond monetizing engagement across our existing services, we are building new experiences and revenue streams around consumer agents.

Mark highlighted the impressive early momentum with Muse. Users have found many reasons to use Muse with the top 3 categories being shopping, personal productivity and creativity. We are encouraged by the breadth of use cases, with shopping in particular being used by over 25% of Muse weekly actives.

While our near-term priority is to grow adoption and expand Muse's reach, we see multiple paths to monetization, beginning with subscriptions.

We also see a significant opportunity to extend Muse to small businesses. Based on a recent user survey, we estimate that at least 500 million self-identified small businesses use Meta's family of apps to reach customers and generate revenue. Muse could help these businesses acquire customers and operate more efficiently, while helping people complete transactions. Over time, consumer and business agents could connect and transact directly, creating opportunities around paid usage, commerce, and business services.

Alongside growth, we are focused on building sustainable unit economics. Muse's compute intensity means that expanding its user base will require significant investment, and we expect total serving costs to rise. At the same time, we expect to improve compute cost efficiency by more than tenfold over the next year, driven by better utilization of off-peak capacity, more efficient models and inference optimization.

As revenue scales, these efficiency gains give us confidence in our ability to build a highly profitable business over time.

Moving now to our financial outlook.

We expect fourth quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $73-76 billion. Our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth, based on current exchange rates.

Turning to the expense and capex outlooks.

We are raising our expense outlook to incorporate the $9.9 billion charge related to legal proceedings recognized in Q3. We now expect full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $175-179 billion.

Excluding the Q3 legal charge, we continue to expect 2026 operating income to be above 2025 operating income.

At a segment level, we now expect Reality Labs losses to decline compared to 2025 to a range of $18-19 billion.

We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $135-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $130-145 billion.

Section: Family of Apps
FoA revenue in the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased $14.01 billion, or 33%, compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was almost entirely driven by advertising revenue.

Advertising

Advertising revenue in the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased $13.63 billion, or 33%, compared to the same period in 2025, due to increases in ad impressions delivered and average price per ad. During the three months ended March 31, 2026, ad impressions delivered increased by 19%, year-over-year, as compared with an increase of 5% in the same period in 2025. Ad impressions delivered during the three months ended March 31, 2026 grew in all regions, especially in Asia-Pacific, which was driven by increases in users and their engagement as well as the frequency of ads shown on our products. During the three months ended March 31, 2026, the average price per ad increased by 12%, year-over-year, as compared with an increase of 10% in the same period in 2025. The increase in average price per ad in the three months ended March 31, 2026 was driven by an increase in advertising demand, which we believe is mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools, and a favorable foreign currency exchange impact. This increase was partially offset by a higher number of ad impressions delivered, especially in geographies and in products, such as Reels, that monetize at lower rates. Other factors are discussed in the section entitled "—Executive Overview of First Quarter Results." In addition, the online commerce vertical was the largest contributor to the increase in advertising revenue in the three months ended March 31, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. We anticipate that future advertising revenue will be driven by a combination of price and ad impressions delivered.

Other revenue

FoA other revenue in the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased $375 million, or 74%, compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was mostly driven by paid messaging from WhatsApp and Meta Verified subscriptions.

[META | FY2026 Q3 | FORM_10Q]
Section: Family of Apps
FoA revenue in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased $13.39 billion, or 26%, and $40.62 billion, or 29%, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025. The increases were almost entirely driven by advertising revenue.

Advertising

Advertising revenue in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased $12.98 billion, or 26%, and $39.41 billion, or 29%, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025, due to increases in ad impressions delivered and average price per ad. During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, ad impressions delivered increased by 10% and 14%, respectively, year-over-year, as compared with increases of 14% and 10%, respectively, in the same periods in 2025. Ad impressions delivered during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 grew in all regions, especially in Asia-Pacific, which was driven by increases in users and their engagement as well as the frequency of ads shown on our products. During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the average price per ad increased by 14% and 13%, respectively, year-over-year, as compared with increases of 10% in both periods in 2025. The increases in average price per ad in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were driven by an increase in advertising demand, which we believe is mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools. A favorable foreign currency exchange impact also contributed to the increase in the nine months ended September 30, 2026. These increases were partially offset by a higher number of ad impressions delivered, especially in geographies and in products, such as Reels, that monetize at lower rates. Other factors are discussed in the section entitled "—Executive Overview of Third Quarter Results." In addition, the online commerce vertical was the largest contributor to the increase in advertising revenue in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025. We anticipate that future advertising revenue will be driven by a combination of price and ad impressions delivered.

Other revenue

FoA other revenue in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased $407 million, or 59%, and $1.20 billion, or 67%, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025. The increases were primarily driven by paid messaging from WhatsApp and subscriptions.

REDMOND, Wash. — October 28, 2026 — Microsoft Corp. today announced the following results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the corresponding period of last fiscal year:

• Revenue was $92.3 billion and increased 19%

• Operating income was $45.9 billion and increased 21% (up 22% in constant currency)

• Net income was $36.6 billion and increased 32% on a GAAP basis, and was $36.4 billion and increased 18% (up 19% in constant currency) on a non-GAAP basis

• Diluted earnings per share was $4.92 and increased 32% on a GAAP basis, and was $4.89 and increased 18% (up 19% in constant currency) on a non-GAAP basis

• Non-GAAP results exclude the impact from investments in OpenAI, explained in the Non-GAAP Definition section below

“We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack,” said Satya Nadella, chairman and chief executive officer of Microsoft. “By helping organizations build and own their own intelligence, and earning trust through agent safety and security, we are translating our innovation into growing adoption and real-world impact across every industry.”

“We delivered a strong start to the fiscal year with Microsoft Cloud revenue of $63.9 billion, with growth accelerating to 30% (up 31% in constant currency) year-over-year,” said Amy Hood, executive vice president and chief financial officer of Microsoft. “Results exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income, and earnings per share.”

The following table adjusts for the impact from investments in OpenAI and reconciles our financial results reported in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) to non-GAAP financial results. Additional information regarding our non-GAAP definition is provided below. All growth comparisons relate to the corresponding period in the last fiscal year.

[MSFT | FY2026 Q3 | FORM_10Q]
Section: Reportable Segments
Productivity and Business Processes

Revenue increased $5.1 billion or 17%.

• Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services revenue increased $3.7 billion or 17%. Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue grew 19% with growth in revenue per user driven by Microsoft 365 E5 and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Microsoft 365 Commercial seats grew 6% driven by small and medium businesses and frontline worker offerings. Microsoft 365 Commercial products revenue grew 1%.

• Microsoft 365 Consumer products and cloud services revenue increased $476 million or 26%. Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue grew 33% driven by growth in revenue per user and Microsoft 365 Consumer subscriber growth of 7%.

• LinkedIn revenue increased $521 million or 12% with growth across all lines of business.

• Dynamics products and cloud services revenue increased $363 million or 19% driven by growth in Dynamics 365. Dynamics 365 revenue grew 22% with growth across all workloads.

Operating income increased $3.6 billion or 21%.

• Cost of revenue increased $680 million or 12% driven by investments in AI infrastructure to support Microsoft 365 Copilot seat and usage growth.

• Gross margin increased $4.4 billion or 18% driven by growth in Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud. Gross margin percentage increased slightly driven by efficiency gains in Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud even with continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage.

• Operating expenses increased $795 million or 11% driven by continued investments in research and development compute capacity, AI talent, and data to support product development that benefits the entire portfolio, as well as higher Copilot advertising expenses.

Revenue, gross margin, and operating income included a favorable foreign currency impact of 4%, 5%, and 7%, respectively. Operating expenses included an unfavorable foreign currency impact of 2%.

Intelligent Cloud

Revenue increased $7.9 billion or 30%.

• Server products and cloud services revenue increased $7.8 billion or 32% driven by Azure and other cloud services. Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 40% driven by demand for services across the platform with continued growth across all workloads. Server products revenue increased slightly, primarily driven by higher purchases of licenses running in multi-cloud environments, offset in part by renewals with lower in-period revenue recognition from the mix of contracts and continued customer shift to cloud.

• Enterprise and partner services revenue increased $141 million or 7% driven by growth in Enterprise Support Services.

Operating income increased $2.7 billion or 24%.

• Cost of revenue increased $4.8 billion or 47% driven by investments in AI infrastructure to support growing customer demand and increased GitHub Copilot usage.

[MSFT | FY2026 Q4 | TRANSCRIPT]
Speaker: AMY HOOD
Growth will again be driven by ARPU and an increase in subscription volume.

For LinkedIn, we expect revenue growth in the high-single digits.

And in Dynamics 365, we expect revenue growth to be in the low-teens, relatively stable quarter-over-quarter driven by continued growth in ERP, although impacted by the bookings trends noted earlier.

For Intelligent Cloud, we expect revenue of $40.95 to $41.25 billion, or growth of 33% to 34%.

In Azure, we expect revenue growth of approximately 45% in constant currency and we remain focused on delivering efficiencies that help us bridge the gaps we see as customer demand continues to exceed supply. Even with the strong close to Q4, we continue to expect H1 growth to accelerate. And as a reminder, year-over-year Azure growth rates can vary quarter-to-quarter based on capacity timing and contract mix.

In our on-premises server business, we expect revenue to decline in the low to mid-single digits, with ongoing customer shift to cloud offerings and the prior-year comparable noted earlier.

In More Personal Computing, we expect revenue to be $12.2 to $12.7 billion as we continue to lap the strong prior-year comparables noted earlier and navigate complex PC market dynamics impacted by component prices and inventory levels.

Windows OEM and Devices revenue should decline in the low twenties driven by the market dynamics noted earlier. As in prior quarters, the range of potential outcomes remains wider than normal.

Search advertising revenue ex-TAC growth should be in the mid-single digits, down sequentially due to the impact of third-party partnerships. Growth will continue to be driven by consistent trends in revenue per search and volume.

And in XBOX content and services, we expect revenue to decline in the mid-single digits. Hardware revenue should decline year-over-year.

Therefore, at the total company level, revenue should be between $89.85 and $90.95 billion or growth of 16% to 17% with accelerating commercial growth partially offset by the impact from the PC market dynamics noted earlier.

We expect COGS of $29.6 to $29.8 billion, or growth of 23% to 24%. And operating expense of $16.8 to $16.9 billion or growth of 7% to 8% driven by continued investment in R&D compute capacity and talent. Operating margins should be relatively flat year-over-year.

Excluding any impact from our investments in OpenAI, other income and expense is expected to be roughly negative $100 million as interest income will be more than offset by interest expense, which includes the interest payments related to datacenter finance leases.

And we expect our Q1 effective tax rate to be approximately 20%.

Next, capital expenditures.

We expect CapEx spend will be over $50 billion including the lease reclassification impact from the useful life update.

[META | FY2026 Q1 | TRANSCRIPT]
Speaker: Susan Li, CFO
Last month, we rolled out our affiliate partnerships offering on Facebook to more test partners, so creators can tag products from participating retailers on their posts and earn a commission when someone makes a purchase. We have also started testing similar experiences on Instagram.

We see a real opportunity to help people more easily discover and buy products within our services, particularly as we incorporate AI deeply across our platforms.

Next, I would like to discuss our approach to capital allocation.

Compute is becoming increasingly important as it determines the quality of the services we can provide, including powering more capable models and delivering innovative new products. It is also becoming more critical to how we work at Meta, as we are entering a world where employees are managing agents to help them generate new ideas, run experiments, execute tasks, and build products.

We are investing aggressively to meet our infrastructure needs and ensure we maximize our strategic flexibility over the coming years. This includes substantially expanding our own data center footprint and striking deals throughout the supply chain to secure necessary components for future capacity. We are also signing cloud deals that will come online over the course of this year and 2027, allowing us to scale more quickly. These multi-year cloud deals and our

infrastructure purchase agreements drove a $107 billion step up in our contractual commitments this quarter.

Our investments will support our training needs for future models, and most importantly, provide us the inference capacity necessary to deliver personal and business agents to billions of people around the world, along with several other AI product experiences we’re developing.

As we grow our infrastructure spend, we remain committed to operating efficiently, and we recently shared internally that we plan to reduce the size of our employee base in May. We believe a leaner operating model will allow us to move more quickly while also helping to offset the substantial investments we’re making.

Moving to our financial outlook.

We expect second quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $58-61 billion. Our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 2% tailwind to year-over-year total revenue growth, based on current exchange rates.

Turning to the expense and capex outlooks.

We expect full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $162-169 billion, unchanged from our prior outlook.

We continue to expect to deliver operating income this year that is above 2025 operating income.

We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $125-145 billion, increased from our prior range of $115-135 billion. This reflects our expectations for higher component pricing this year and, to a lesser extent, additional data center costs to support future year capacity.

Absent any changes to our tax landscape, we expect our tax rate for the remaining quarters of 2026 to be between 13-16%.

[META | FY2026 Q2 | PRESS_RELEASE]
Section: Meta Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
MENLO PARK, Calif. – July 29, 2026 – Meta Platforms, Inc. (Nasdaq: META) today reported financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.

"AI is accelerating our core business today, powering our next generation of products, and opening the door to entirely new enterprise opportunities," said Mark Zuckerberg, Meta founder and CEO. "The results are already showing, and I'm optimistic about the potential ahead."

[META | FY2026 Q3 | TRANSCRIPT]
Speaker: Susan Li, CFO
Meta One is rolling out gradually with more than 50

features across Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp, including Meta Business Agent and Meta AI, and has surpassed 15 million subscriptions and trials to date. The core experience across our apps and Meta AI will remain free, while subscriptions offer more specialized capabilities and expanded AI usage.

Beyond monetizing engagement across our existing services, we are building new experiences and revenue streams around consumer agents.

Mark highlighted the impressive early momentum with Muse. Users have found many reasons to use Muse with the top 3 categories being shopping, personal productivity and creativity. We are encouraged by the breadth of use cases, with shopping in particular being used by over 25% of Muse weekly actives.

While our near-term priority is to grow adoption and expand Muse's reach, we see multiple paths to monetization, beginning with subscriptions.

We also see a significant opportunity to extend Muse to small businesses. Based on a recent user survey, we estimate that at least 500 million self-identified small businesses use Meta's family of apps to reach customers and generate revenue. Muse could help these businesses acquire customers and operate more efficiently, while helping people complete transactions. Over time, consumer and business agents could connect and transact directly, creating opportunities around paid usage, commerce, and business services.

Alongside growth, we are focused on building sustainable unit economics. Muse's compute intensity means that expanding its user base will require significant investment, and we expect total serving costs to rise. At the same time, we expect to improve compute cost efficiency by more than tenfold over the next year, driven by better utilization of off-peak capacity, more efficient models and inference optimization.

As revenue scales, these efficiency gains give us confidence in our ability to build a highly profitable business over time.

Moving now to our financial outlook.

We expect fourth quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $73-76 billion. Our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth, based on current exchange rates.

Turning to the expense and capex outlooks.

We are raising our expense outlook to incorporate the $9.9 billion charge related to legal proceedings recognized in Q3. We now expect full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $175-179 billion.

Excluding the Q3 legal charge, we continue to expect 2026 operating income to be above 2025 operating income.

At a segment level, we now expect Reality Labs losses to decline compared to 2025 to a range of $18-19 billion.

We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $135-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $130-145 billion.

We estimate that advertisers who adopted its recommendations drove almost 5% more conversions at the same cost per conversion and increased their advertising investment by 9% compared with similar non-adopters. We are rolling out additional capabilities, including creative insights, stronger business context and more agentic actions. These features will allow marketers to plan, create and optimize campaigns, as well as schedule tasks and alerts, through a conversational experience with approvals and previews that keep them in control.

I’ll share one example of how Meta AI business assistant is empowering our advertisers. Simply Organic Maple, a family-run maple syrup producer in Vermont, used Meta AI business assistant to improve its campaign messaging. After the business assistant recommended testing longer, more descriptive advertising copy, the business saw a 57% increase in purchases and a 36% reduction in cost per purchase. Its strongest revised ad delivered a 3x return on ad spend, a 52% improvement from the original.

Adoption of our generative AI ad creative tools also continues to scale. In Q3, nearly 10 million advertisers used at least one of these tools. Advertiser adoption of our video generation features grew 25% quarter-over-quarter, driven in part by ready-made videos that reduce generation time to just a few seconds from a single image upload.

We're also expanding the opportunity at the intersection of creators and advertising.

Partnership Ads, which allow advertisers to run ads with creators, brands and other businesses, continued to scale rapidly in Q3. Our partnership ads product grew over 97% year-over-year and surpassed $15 billion in annual revenue run-rate.

In Q3, we also completed the global rollout of Creator Marketing Hub to all advertisers, bringing creator discovery, content organization and partnership ad activation into one place, with more than 10 million creators now discoverable. We are integrating Meta AI Business Assistant into the Hub so advertisers can conversationally search for creators, identify content to use in partnership ads and get guidance across their creator marketing workflows.

Outside of ads, we are also building out additional ways to monetize engagement across our ecosystem.

In September, we announced the global expansion of Meta One, our unified subscription service for consumers, creators and businesses. Meta One is rolling out gradually with more than 50

features across Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp, including Meta Business Agent and Meta AI, and has surpassed 15 million subscriptions and trials to date. The core experience across our apps and Meta AI will remain free, while subscriptions offer more specialized capabilities and expanded AI usage.

Beyond monetizing engagement across our existing services, we are building new experiences and revenue streams around consumer agents.

Section: Family of Apps
FoA revenue in the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased $14.01 billion, or 33%, compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was almost entirely driven by advertising revenue.

Advertising

Advertising revenue in the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased $13.63 billion, or 33%, compared to the same period in 2025, due to increases in ad impressions delivered and average price per ad. During the three months ended March 31, 2026, ad impressions delivered increased by 19%, year-over-year, as compared with an increase of 5% in the same period in 2025. Ad impressions delivered during the three months ended March 31, 2026 grew in all regions, especially in Asia-Pacific, which was driven by increases in users and their engagement as well as the frequency of ads shown on our products. During the three months ended March 31, 2026, the average price per ad increased by 12%, year-over-year, as compared with an increase of 10% in the same period in 2025. The increase in average price per ad in the three months ended March 31, 2026 was driven by an increase in advertising demand, which we believe is mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools, and a favorable foreign currency exchange impact. This increase was partially offset by a higher number of ad impressions delivered, especially in geographies and in products, such as Reels, that monetize at lower rates. Other factors are discussed in the section entitled "—Executive Overview of First Quarter Results." In addition, the online commerce vertical was the largest contributor to the increase in advertising revenue in the three months ended March 31, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. We anticipate that future advertising revenue will be driven by a combination of price and ad impressions delivered.

Other revenue

FoA other revenue in the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased $375 million, or 74%, compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was mostly driven by paid messaging from WhatsApp and Meta Verified subscriptions.

Now, before I move to outlook, effective at the start of FY27, we are extending the estimated useful lives of our datacenters and office buildings, from 15 to 25 years, reflecting our operating history and expected use of these assets. The impact of this update is reflected in today's guidance.

question: What is Muse and how did Meta describe its launch in Q3 2026?
goldAnswer: Muse is Meta's personal agent, the product form of its personal superintelligence vision; one of its most successful launches ever.
answer:
**FY2026 Q3**

In Q3 2026, Meta launched Muse, a personal agent designed to deliver personal superintelligence to users. The launch was described as one of their most successful, with over 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada setting up Muse personal agents within the first six weeks. Engagement and retention rates were reported to be strong, with about 25% of users engaging with Muse daily, which is more than double the initial engagement levels seen with other AI apps like Threads [4][9].

The most common use cases for Muse included shopping, personal productivity, and creativity, with over 25% of weekly active users engaging in shopping activities. The average purchase size for shopping through Muse was reported to be over $200 [2][4][10]. 

Meta's CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, emphasized the importance of building a large-scale Muse network, which they believe will enhance the value of the service as more users and businesses participate [16].

[META | FY2026 Q3 | TRANSCRIPT]
Speaker: Mark Zuckerberg, CEO
And in the first week we had to work with Stripe to raise credit limits since the volumes were above what any of us expected.

Beyond shopping, the most common connectors are for personal productivity and connecting Muse to your other services like email and calendar. This shows the importance of the Muse Secure VM that we've built to provide state-of-the-art privacy and security, and we're looking forward to following up soon with the Muse Confidential VM, which will make it so that even Meta cannot see your content.

We have also seen that Muse Wonder improves quality, engagement, and retention further, which suggests that as we continue to improve intelligence, Muse will perform better and better over time.

Now that Muse has clear product-market fit, we're entering a new phase and a more operational phase that is focused on scaling it. The goals of this next phase play to many of Meta's strengths. We need to do three things: scale the product, grow revenue, and optimize compute costs.

We expect to grow Muse to serve billions of people. This is both our mission and our strategy. It's our mission in that we believe in putting the power of personal superintelligence in everyone's hands. We believe that that is the path to ensuring a positive future for everyone with individual empowerment as the source of prosperity and balance of power as the foundation for safety. On a values level, we believe that delivering this capability widely is the best thing that we can be doing. This is also our strategy, because we think that billions of Muses in a network at scale will be able to get more done for people and businesses by working together. So we'd like to create a large scale Muse network as quickly as possible.

From a business perspective, the average revenue per American user for our existing Family of Apps users is several hundreds of dollars annually, and we expect that Muse will reach an even higher level over time due to the amount of commerce that we already see taking place. This will take some time, but we're starting to work on this now. Our business model will have a few components:

For most people, the product should be free and we will build commerce tools so we get paid a fee based on the transactions that we help facilitate. We expect this will be paid for by businesses.

For people who want the most advanced models or to use extra tokens, they subscribe directly and pay.

For business owners who want additional features to use Muse to grow their businesses or for companies that want people to use Muse for work, they will be able to subscribe directly and pay as well.

And for those who want Muse to help improve the personalization and quality of their content and ads across Meta, they will be able to connect to those experiences as well.

Just to clarify, the average revenue that I was talking about before is the Family of Apps revenue for our existing Muse users.

Meta One is rolling out gradually with more than 50

features across Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp, including Meta Business Agent and Meta AI, and has surpassed 15 million subscriptions and trials to date. The core experience across our apps and Meta AI will remain free, while subscriptions offer more specialized capabilities and expanded AI usage.

Beyond monetizing engagement across our existing services, we are building new experiences and revenue streams around consumer agents.

Mark highlighted the impressive early momentum with Muse. Users have found many reasons to use Muse with the top 3 categories being shopping, personal productivity and creativity. We are encouraged by the breadth of use cases, with shopping in particular being used by over 25% of Muse weekly actives.

While our near-term priority is to grow adoption and expand Muse's reach, we see multiple paths to monetization, beginning with subscriptions.

We also see a significant opportunity to extend Muse to small businesses. Based on a recent user survey, we estimate that at least 500 million self-identified small businesses use Meta's family of apps to reach customers and generate revenue. Muse could help these businesses acquire customers and operate more efficiently, while helping people complete transactions. Over time, consumer and business agents could connect and transact directly, creating opportunities around paid usage, commerce, and business services.

Alongside growth, we are focused on building sustainable unit economics. Muse's compute intensity means that expanding its user base will require significant investment, and we expect total serving costs to rise. At the same time, we expect to improve compute cost efficiency by more than tenfold over the next year, driven by better utilization of off-peak capacity, more efficient models and inference optimization.

As revenue scales, these efficiency gains give us confidence in our ability to build a highly profitable business over time.

Moving now to our financial outlook.

We expect fourth quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $73-76 billion. Our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth, based on current exchange rates.

Turning to the expense and capex outlooks.

We are raising our expense outlook to incorporate the $9.9 billion charge related to legal proceedings recognized in Q3. We now expect full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $175-179 billion.

Excluding the Q3 legal charge, we continue to expect 2026 operating income to be above 2025 operating income.

At a segment level, we now expect Reality Labs losses to decline compared to 2025 to a range of $18-19 billion.

We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $135-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $130-145 billion.

And for those who want Muse to help improve the personalization and quality of their content and ads across Meta, they will be able to connect to those experiences as well.

Just to clarify, the average revenue that I was talking about before is the Family of Apps revenue for our existing Muse users.

On the compute side, we are building out the capacity to serve more than a billion people over the next few years. In the near term, Muse is very compute-intensive to run. But we expect to improve its cost efficiency by more than 10x in the next year, which will enable it to be profitable once the revenue lines are at scale. If compute efficiency continues improving quickly for another few years, which we think is highly likely, then Muse will be highly profitable over multiple years. In the near term, the strength of our core business enables us to scale the Muse network before then. And we believe that we are the best positioned company to pursue this strategy.

One other note on compute economics is that since training is a large fixed cost, now that we have leading models, we want to serve as much high-margin inference demand as possible. That is why we are building the Meta Enterprise Platform, led by CJ Desai. Muse Wonder and even more advanced models that we are training can serve additional high-margin services beyond the Muse network, including our API, Muse Code, and other enterprise services.

A fundamental feature of our business is that we have many good uses for this compute. It is difficult to forecast the exact growth rates for the Muse network, for our enterprise platform, and for how Muse Wonder and beyond will accelerate our core business. But through building out multiple ways to deploy these advanced models, we increase the chances that one or more of them significantly outperforms our expectations. Beyond serving other businesses, we have not yet found the limit of how effectively we can apply compute to accelerating our own core business. We have implemented an eval with Muse Wonder to improve how effectively it can autonomously improve our recommendations and ads systems. And as our upcoming models get even more advanced, I expect that we’re going to see an increasing rate of improvement in these systems.

Alright, let's talk about the models now. Muse Wonder is state-of-the-art across many dimensions that matter for personal superintelligence. This validates the importance of training models ourselves to deliver the best experience. In addition to Muse, we've also seen that engagement per person in Meta AI has more than doubled since April when we started rolling out our new models.

Hey everyone. Thanks for joining today.

This has been a busy and exciting few months. Our family of apps is now used by 3.64 billion people each day, and we're seeing all-time highs in engagement on both Facebook and Instagram driven by strong growth in video. Threads has now overtaken X in monthly actives and continues to grow quickly. WhatsApp is hitting all-time highs in messaging and is becoming an increasingly important platform for agents as well.

In the last few months we have had several major milestones towards our goal of delivering personal superintelligence to everyone. We had one of our most successful launches ever with the Muse personal agent; we shipped Muse Wonder as our first frontier model; and we shipped several new glasses and gadgets with Muse integration, including coming soon to our new audio glasses.

We have been discussing our vision for personal superintelligence for more than a year now. We want to help every person have an extremely capable personal agent that understands your goals and can help you achieve them and improve your life in whatever ways you want -- whether that's improving your relationships, helping you save time, save money, build a business, create new things, or anything else that you can dream of. Muse is the product form of this vision. So now we have the foundational technology in place to deliver this. There is still a lot of work ahead, but our initial position is very strong.

In just a month and a half, more than 10 million people in the US and Canada have set up Muse personal agents. Growth continues to be strong and we have been #1 in the App Store almost every day. Engagement and retention are also off to a strong start. About 25% of people who have set up Muse use it on any given day. For our earliest adopters, the longer that they use Muse,

the better that retention seems to get. To put this in perspective, this is more than twice the level that Threads started at or where we believe that other AI apps started at as well.

The most common use case for Muse is shopping, with more than a quarter of people who are using Muse engaging in this with an average purchase size over $200. Plaid told us they hadn't seen activity like they're seeing with their connector on any other service before. And in the first week we had to work with Stripe to raise credit limits since the volumes were above what any of us expected.

Beyond shopping, the most common connectors are for personal productivity and connecting Muse to your other services like email and calendar. This shows the importance of the Muse Secure VM that we've built to provide state-of-the-art privacy and security, and we're looking forward to following up soon with the Muse Confidential VM, which will make it so that even Meta cannot see your content.
sources.speaker: Mark Zuckerberg, CEO

sources.content:
[META | FY2026 Q3 | TRANSCRIPT]
Speaker: Mark Zuckerberg, CEO
And as our upcoming models get even more advanced, I expect that we’re going to see an increasing rate of improvement in these systems.

Alright, let's talk about the models now. Muse Wonder is state-of-the-art across many dimensions that matter for personal superintelligence. This validates the importance of training models ourselves to deliver the best experience. In addition to Muse, we've also seen that engagement per person in Meta AI has more than doubled since April when we started rolling out our new models.

While Muse Wonder has been our most important release, I've been very pleased with our pace of execution here. In the last few months we've shipped Muse Spark 1.2 and 1.3, Muse Code, two open weights models with Muse Glimmer and Muse Spark Open, and also Muse Voice.

Going forward, with the field advancing quickly, we plan to focus on both pushing the frontier of intelligence and distilling those models into much smaller and more efficient product models that will be optimized for personal agents. My view is that we will be able to build superintelligence through scaling, so we are methodically working our way up the ladder there. We are already working on larger models after Muse Wonder, and they're going to be very impressive and capable. We’re also working on new smaller models that are coming out soon that will deliver Muse Wonder-level intelligence more efficiently.

Moving on, our work on personal superintelligence is now also the focus of Reality Labs. Muse is coming to Meta Glasses starting next month, and that will be an important step towards this. People already love many features of the glasses already -- music, calling, capturing moments,

hearing assistance, and more -- but over time we expect Muse and having your personal superintelligence with you throughout the day will be the most important part of the experience.

Muse is also central to the business model for the glasses. Again, our mission and strategy are to serve everyone here. We believe in putting the power of this technology in everyone's hands. So we have priced our devices not to make a large profit on the hardware, but to build a large software and superintelligence business on top of them over time. Glasses sales continue to grow rapidly, and now with Muse, we expect that paid subscriptions will increase and that this business will begin improving meaningfully from here.

I also shared at Connect that we are changing our approach to virtual reality to only ship new devices when we have major breakthroughs like we had with the Meta VR Glasses this year -- which of course are the first VR experience ever in a pair of glasses. I continue to believe that the path to delivering the holographic experience of bringing together the physical and digital worlds in everyday glasses will come through VR first, but we will pace this aspect of our investment more to focus on delivering personal superintelligence first.

That's why I mentioned that we launched Muse first on Muse Spark, and that's what is currently the default across the free tier. And we rolled out Muse Wonder, and people can access that in the paid tier today. And we know that it performs a

lot better, so we're working on getting a more efficient version of Muse Wonder that we'll be able to roll out more broadly.

But you can imagine just as we iterate forward in two, three models into the future, when you have significantly higher intelligence and capability to solve many more problems for people and the ability to deliver that at a much more affordable price point, I think that that's going to just unlock a lot more value to people. So we're very excited about that.

Transitioning to talking about the enterprise piece because I think these two pieces, there is some connection here in that the main enterprise offering in the near term is going to be the model API and Muse Code. And we have business agents that we've been scaling for a while, and each of those three things is growing quite quickly. So we're excited about that.

Over time we would like to make it so that we have a whole kind of business network of Muse agents as well.

There's the business agent which we've talked about on previous earnings calls for businesses to help out with sales and customer support.

But what we see is a lot of people are actually using Muse today to help run especially small businesses. And we think that there's both an opportunity to help create an agent that people use to really enable them to automate and do a lot of the parts of spinning up a small business that are just kind of difficult and time consuming but aren't the core thing that a person is trying to do.

So we think that's a big deal. And then making a version of Muse that people can bring into different corporate environments and work there, we think is going to be a big deal.

And then beyond that, building what I refer to as the Muse network which is making it so that Muse is not just a kind of single player game where you have your Muse but making it so that your Muses can work with your friends and your families. And if you want to buy something, it's not just navigating to that business' website. It's talking to their agent. I think that getting that all to work well together is going to unlock tremendous value at scale.

So I'm very excited about all of that. I think the enterprise use is going to be a big part of it, but it's also going to kind of have this very valuable boost in the utility for consumers, too. So I'm very excited about both of those.

We -- the compute efficiency work is going to be important on this also because we want to make sure that we've built enough compute to be able to serve what we think is going to be 1 billion plus people if we can achieve certain compute efficiency targets, but we obviously have a lot of work to do there as well. And that will be one of the limiting factors over the next year.

We want to build out the business around it. So I talked about that. We estimate that advertisers who adopted its recommendations drove almost 5% more conversions at the same cost per conversion and increased their advertising investment by 9% compared with similar non-adopters. We are rolling out additional capabilities, including creative insights, stronger business context and more agentic actions. These features will allow marketers to plan, create and optimize campaigns, as well as schedule tasks and alerts, through a conversational experience with approvals and previews that keep them in control.

I’ll share one example of how Meta AI business assistant is empowering our advertisers. Simply Organic Maple, a family-run maple syrup producer in Vermont, used Meta AI business assistant to improve its campaign messaging. After the business assistant recommended testing longer, more descriptive advertising copy, the business saw a 57% increase in purchases and a 36% reduction in cost per purchase. Its strongest revised ad delivered a 3x return on ad spend, a 52% improvement from the original.

Adoption of our generative AI ad creative tools also continues to scale. In Q3, nearly 10 million advertisers used at least one of these tools. Advertiser adoption of our video generation features grew 25% quarter-over-quarter, driven in part by ready-made videos that reduce generation time to just a few seconds from a single image upload.

We're also expanding the opportunity at the intersection of creators and advertising.

Partnership Ads, which allow advertisers to run ads with creators, brands and other businesses, continued to scale rapidly in Q3. Our partnership ads product grew over 97% year-over-year and surpassed $15 billion in annual revenue run-rate.

In Q3, we also completed the global rollout of Creator Marketing Hub to all advertisers, bringing creator discovery, content organization and partnership ad activation into one place, with more than 10 million creators now discoverable. We are integrating Meta AI Business Assistant into the Hub so advertisers can conversationally search for creators, identify content to use in partnership ads and get guidance across their creator marketing workflows.

Outside of ads, we are also building out additional ways to monetize engagement across our ecosystem.

In September, we announced the global expansion of Meta One, our unified subscription service for consumers, creators and businesses. Meta One is rolling out gradually with more than 50

features across Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp, including Meta Business Agent and Meta AI, and has surpassed 15 million subscriptions and trials to date. The core experience across our apps and Meta AI will remain free, while subscriptions offer more specialized capabilities and expanded AI usage.

Beyond monetizing engagement across our existing services, we are building new experiences and revenue streams around consumer agents.

Section: Other Actions
We filed a petition for a writ of certiorari with the U.S. Supreme Court on October 2, 2024, which was denied. We then moved to compel arbitration, which the district court denied. We appealed the denial of our motion to compel arbitration to the Ninth Circuit on December 3, 2025. The matter is stayed in district court pending resolution of our appeal.

Beginning on July 7, 2023, multiple cases, including putative class actions, were filed against us in the United States and elsewhere, alleging that we improperly acquired, distributed, and used various copyrighted materials and/or other types of data to train our artificial intelligence models and seeking unspecified damages and injunctive relief. In the United States, statutory damages for copyright liability are calculated on a per work basis, which may result in substantial damages, particularly given the large volumes of data required to train AI models. The cases in the United States, which were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California (Kadrey, et al. v. Meta Platforms, Inc., Chabon, et al. v. Meta Platforms, Inc. and Farnsworth v. Meta Platforms, Inc.) and U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (Huckabee, et al. v. Meta Platforms, Inc. et al., which was subsequently transferred to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California), have been consolidated into Kadrey, et al. v. Meta Platforms, Inc. Motions for summary judgment were heard in this case on May 1, 2025, including on the issue of the applicability of the fair use defense to use of copyrighted books for generative AI model training. On June 25, 2025, the court granted our motion for summary judgment on fair use as to the named plaintiffs in the case. The parties will proceed to brief the remaining claims of copyright infringement and contributory infringement related to alleged distribution of books to third parties during the downloading process. Let’s begin with our segment results. All comparisons are on a year-over-year basis unless otherwise noted.

Q3 Total Family of Apps revenue was $64.2 billion, up 26%.

Q3 Family of Apps ad revenue was $63.1 billion, up 26% on both a reported and constant currency basis.

In Q3, the total number of ad impressions served across our services increased 10%. Impression growth was healthy across all regions, driven by growth in engagement and users, as well as ad

load optimizations. The global average price per ad increased 14% year-over-year, driven by ad performance gains and improvements in macro conditions relative to Q3 of last year. This was partially offset by strong impression growth, particularly from lower-monetizing surfaces and regions.

Family of Apps other revenue was $1.1 billion and grew 59%, driven primarily by WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions revenue.

Within our Reality Labs segment, Q3 revenue was $443 million, down 6% due to lower Quest headset sales, which were partially offset by continued strong growth in AI glasses revenue.

Moving now to our consolidated results.

Q3 total revenue was $64.6 billion, up 26% on both a reported and constant currency basis.

Q3 total expenses were $51.6 billion, up 68% compared to last year, and included a $9.9 billion charge related to the August 2026 multistate attorneys general agreement. Year-over-year growth was primarily driven by legal-related costs, infrastructure costs, and third-party AI token costs.

The growth in infrastructure costs was driven by higher third party cloud spend, depreciation, and data center operating costs.

We ended Q3 with over 66,000 employees, down 12% from Q2 following the May 2026 headcount reduction.

Third quarter GAAP operating income was $13.0 billion, representing a 37% decline year-over- year and a 20% operating margin. Excluding the Q3 legal charges related to the aforementioned legal settlement, our third quarter operating income would have increased 11% year-over-year.

Our tax rate for the quarter was 24%, above our outlook range primarily driven by the non- deductible portion of legal expenses.

Net income was $9.9 billion or $3.83 per share.

Capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $34.9 billion, driven by investments in servers, data centers, and network infrastructure.

Free cash flow was negative $2.1 billion. We ended the quarter with $82.4 billion in cash and marketable securities and $83.7 billion in debt.

[GOOGL | FY2026 Q3 | TRANSCRIPT]
Section: 2026 Q3 Earnings Call
Speaker: Thomas Kurian, SVP and CEO, Google Cloud
Eric, on the demand in Cloud, we are always managing our portfolio to ensure we have a breadth of customers; and we have different types of customers from digital natives, AI labs, traditional enterprises, financial and capital markets customers, so it's a broad set of customers.

Many of them have either started with using TPU systems, for example, in our Cloud. We have over a hundred significant TPU customers who start in our Cloud, they learn to use TPUs; and remember, a TPU system is a combination of hardware, system software, compilers, the whole thing, assembled as a system, including optical networking and other things.

We have taken a very deliberate approach on how we're bringing TPUs to customers. The first one is to build the right silicon, so we have 8t for training, 8i for inference. They both offer substantial price performance and performance improvements relative to prior generations.

Second, we've optimized the software. The optimization of the software is not just to make the systems run better and to give you great performance, but also to make portability seamless.

Recently, we introduced, for example, Pytorch, which opens up a much larger market for us by optimizing Pytorch on the TPU.

Third, we are broadening distribution. So, in the past, you could use TPUs in our Cloud. Now we make, for customers who want TPU systems in their data centers, we're making TPU systems available in their data centers.

We're also broadening availability to other providers. For example, we announced a partnership with Oracle, and we've launched, along with Blackstone, an agreement for Crux AI, a joint venture, to offer customers TPU systems.

We are seeing extraordinary demand, and strong growth from both AI labs, capital markets, financial service institutions, and Enterprises. And if you imagine these hundred-plus customers growing to many more, and also scaling their use into TPU systems, we see strong demand over the future.

On TPU systems and margins, we don't break out margins for individual products or infrastructure components. However, we see several benefits from designing and manufacturing TPU systems.

So first of all, to remind you, the TPU system is not just a chip, but it's a complete system.

Given the price performance benefits of TPU systems relative to competitors, growing demand for accelerated compute and the scarcity of accelerated compute, we are very focused on continuing to improve margins as we scale the business.

Two additional points.

First of all, when Anat mentioned that we procure components to build inventory, we only do that after we have signed contracts, so all of the inventory for TPU systems are associated with committed contracts.

Additionally, by putting TPU systems in third-party facilities and in customer data centers, it allows us, one, to broaden our addressable markets. For some industries, they have data in their premise that they cannot move to a cloud, and it allows us to bring accelerated compute to where the data sits.

Additionally, it also offsets the need for us to have to prebuild facilities to host these TPU systems.

Let me combine these two questions. First, obviously, we don't provide specific financials at the product level, but let me walk through how to think about the financials associated with the TPU system sales.

And obviously, just as a reminder, and Thomas can elaborate on that as well, a TPU system is not just a chip, but it's a specialized system that combines multiple things, including hardware, compute, storage, networking. So we are selling much more than just a chip. Software, training, inference -- there is a significant added value that's being provided to the customer that's purchasing a TPU system.

And the way this works, and this is linked to your second portion of the question, when we sign an agreement with a customer to sell TPU systems, once we sign that agreement, you'll first see that showing up in our backlog. And then we start building inventory. So think about this from a CapEx versus cash perspective.

We build the inventory ahead of getting the revenue stream in. So I think I've alluded to this on the previous call. You see inventory balances go up, where previously inventory balances primarily were some of our hardware products. Now those TPU systems that are not yet sold will be showing up; so you see cash going out, and we're building up the inventory base.

And then as we start delivering and billing customers for these TPU systems, then you see cash coming in. So it's not the traditional kind of CapEx as you're thinking about this, and I think that's the essence of your question, but rather a different cycle of cash flow generation.

Now, given that we are in the process of building up and ramping up that business, you're seeing that cash needs in our cash flow statements, and you see those inventory builds, to date we've had some system sales recorded as revenue, but expect more of it to come in through 2027.

Alphabet Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results

MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif. – October 28, 2026 – Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOG, GOOGL) today announced financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

•Consolidated Alphabet revenues increased 25% to $127.6 billion, reflecting strong performance across the business and our 13th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth.

•Google Cloud delivered record growth as revenues increased 103% to $30.7 billion, led by strong growth in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across enterprise AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions, as well as core GCP services. TPU systems sales were also a meaningful contributor to revenue growth.

•Consolidated Alphabet operating income increased 30% and operating margin was 31.8%.

•Net income available to common stockholders was $26.2 billion and EPS was $2.12.

Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, said:

“We had a strong quarter and are now on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate. Our deep full stack approach is driving momentum across the business, with Alphabet revenues growing 25% year-over year.

Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries. In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years.

Google Cloud revenues grew 103%, powered by huge demand for our AI infrastructure and AI solutions. We’re also seeing strong demand for our TPU systems across a wide range of customers.

Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon are now leading at the frontier. Overall, our first-party model APIs are now processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times what we processed a year ago.

On top of that, the Gemini app has reached one billion users—making it the fastest-growing product in Google’s history—and we surpassed 150 million YouTube Music and Premium subscribers globally, including trials.

We’re excited by the range of big opportunities ahead of us.”

M365 consumer cloud revenue growth should be in the mid to high-twenty percent range driven by growth in ARPU as well as continued subscription volume.

For LinkedIn, we expect revenue growth in the low-double digits.

And in Dynamics 365, we expect revenue growth to be in the high teens with continued growth across all workloads.

For Intelligent Cloud, we expect revenue of $34.1 to $34.4 billion, or growth of 27% to 29%.

In Azure, we expect Q3 revenue growth to be between 37% and 38% in constant currency against a prior year comparable that included significantly accelerating growth rates in both Q3 and Q4. As mentioned earlier, demand continues to exceed supply and we will need to continue to balance the incoming supply we can allocate here against other priorities. As a reminder, there can be quarterly variability in year-on-year growth rates depending on the timing of capacity delivery and when it comes online, as well as from in-period revenue recognition depending on the mix of contracts.

In our on-premises server business, we expect revenue to decline in the low-single digits as growth rates normalize following the launch of SQL Server 2025, though increased memory pricing could create additional volatility in transactional purchasing.

In More Personal Computing, we expect revenue to be $12.3 to $12.8 billion.

Windows OEM and Devices revenue should decline in the low teens. Growth rates will be impacted as the benefit from Windows 10 end of support normalizes and as elevated inventory levels come down through the quarter. Therefore, Windows OEM revenue should decline roughly 10 percent. The range of potential outcomes remains wider than normal, in part due to the potential impact on the PC market from increased memory pricing.

Search and news advertising ex-TAC revenue growth should be in the high single digits. Even as we work to improve execution, we expect continued share gains across Bing and Edge, with growth driven by volume. And we expect sequential growth moderation as the contribution from third-party partnerships continues to normalize.

Section: Valuation
In general, and where applicable, we use quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities to determine the fair value of our financial instruments. This pricing methodology applies to our Level 1 investments, such as U.S. government securities, common and preferred stock, and mutual funds. If quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities are not available to determine fair value, then we use quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities or inputs other than the quoted prices that are observable either directly or indirectly. This pricing methodology applies to our Level 2 investments, such as commercial paper, certificates of deposit, U.S. agency securities, foreign government bonds, mortgage- and asset-backed securities, corporate notes and bonds, and municipal securities. Level 3 investments are valued using internally-developed models with unobservable inputs. Assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis using unobservable inputs are an immaterial portion of our portfolio.

A majority of our investments are priced by pricing vendors and are generally Level 1 or Level 2 investments as these vendors either provide a quoted market price in an active market or use observable inputs for their pricing without applying significant adjustments. Broker pricing is used mainly when a quoted price is not available, the investment is not priced by our pricing vendors, or when a broker price is more reflective of fair values in the market in which the investment trades. Our broker-priced investments are generally classified as Level 2 investments because the broker prices these investments based on similar assets without applying significant adjustments. In addition, all our broker-priced investments have a sufficient level of trading volume to demonstrate that the fair values used are appropriate for these investments. Our fair value processes include controls that are designed to ensure appropriate fair values are recorded. These controls include model validation, review of key model inputs, analysis of period-over-period fluctuations, and independent recalculation of prices where appropriate.
